title.zh: 卷43 列傳第35 李延孫 韋祐 韓雄 陳忻 魏玄
title.en: Volume 43 Biographies 35: Li Yansun; Wei You; Han Xiong; Chen Xin; Wei Xuan
title.raw: 卷43 列傳第35 李延孫 韋祐 韓雄 陳忻 魏玄 Volume 43 Biographies 35: Li Yansun; Wei You; Han Xiong; Chen Xin; Wei Xuan

sentences.zh: 李延孫 韋祐 韓雄 陳忻 魏玄

translations.literal: Li Yansun; Wei You; Han Xiong; Chen Xin; Wei Xuan
translations.idiomatic: Biographies of Li Yansun, Wei You, Han Xiong, Chen Xin, and Wei Xuan

sentences.zh: 李延孫，伊川人也。

translations.literal: Li Yansun was a native of Yichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yansun came from Yichuan.

sentences.zh: 祖伯扶，魏太和末，從征懸瓠有功，為汝南郡守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Bofu, at the end of the Taihe era of Wei, followed the campaign against Xuanchi with merit and became Administrator of Runan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Bofu distinguished himself in the late Taihe campaigns against Xuanchi and was appointed administrator of Runan commandery.

sentences.zh: 父長壽，性雄豪，有武藝。

translations.literal: His father Changshou was by nature bold and heroic and possessed martial skill.
translations.idiomatic: His father Changshou was a bold, formidable man skilled in arms.

sentences.zh: 少與蠻酋結託，屢相招引，侵滅關南。

translations.literal: In his youth he formed ties with barbarian chiefs, repeatedly leading each other in raids, encroaching upon and ravaging the region south of the passes.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he allied with tribal chieftains and repeatedly led them in raids that ravaged the lands south of the passes.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，朝議恐其為亂，乃以長壽為防蠻都督，給其鼓節，以慰其意。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang period the court deliberation feared he would cause disorder, and therefore appointed Changshou Commander for Barbarian Defense, granting him drums and credentials of office to appease his mind.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiaochang era the court, fearing he would stir up rebellion, appointed Changshou commander for the defense against the tribes and bestowed on him drums and credentials of authority to win him over.

sentences.zh: 長壽冀因此遂得任用，亦盡其智力，防遏群蠻。

translations.literal: Changshou hoped that through this he would obtain employment, and also exerted all his intelligence and strength to defend against and restrain the various barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Changshou hoped this would lead to formal employment, and he threw all his wit and energy into holding the tribal peoples in check.

sentences.zh: 伊川左右，寇盜為之稍息。

translations.literal: On both sides of Yichuan, bandits and robbers for this reason gradually subsided.
translations.idiomatic: Around Yichuan, raiding and banditry eased somewhat as a result.

sentences.zh: 永安之後，盜賊蜂起，長壽乃招集叛亡，徒侶日盛。

translations.literal: After the Yong'an era bandits rose like bees; Changshou then gathered deserters and fugitives, and his followers grew day by day.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yong'an period unrest spread like swarming bees; Changshou gathered deserters and fugitives until his following grew daily.

sentences.zh: 魏帝藉其力用，因而撫之。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor relied on his strength and usefulness and accordingly placated him.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor valued his strength and made a point of keeping him on side.

sentences.zh: 乃授持節、大都督，轉鎮張白塢。

translations.literal: He was then granted bearing-the-staff credentials and the title of grand commander-in-chief and transferred to garrison Zhangbaiwu.
translations.idiomatic: He received the insignia of a commissioner with plenipotentiary powers and the rank of grand commander-in-chief, and was posted to garrison Zhangbaiwu.

sentences.zh: 後為河北郡守，轉河內郡守。

translations.literal: Later he became Administrator of Hebei Commandery, then transferred to Administrator of Henei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as administrator of Hebei commandery and then of Henei.

sentences.zh: 所歷之處，咸以猛烈聞。

translations.literal: Every place he passed through was known for his fierceness.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served, he was known for his ruthless severity.

sentences.zh: 討捕諸賊，頻有功。

translations.literal: In pursuing and capturing various bandits he frequently had merit.
translations.idiomatic: His campaigns against bandits brought him repeated credit.

sentences.zh: 授衛大將軍、北華州刺史，賜爵清河郡公。

translations.literal: He was appointed General of the Guard and Governor of Beihua Province and enfeoffed as Duke of Qinghe Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General of the Guard and governor of Beihua province and enfeoffed as Duke of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 及魏孝武西遷，長壽率勵義士拒東魏。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, Changshou led and encouraged loyal men to resist Eastern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei withdrew to the west, Changshou rallied loyal volunteers to resist Eastern Wei.

sentences.zh: 孝武嘉之，復授潁川郡守，遷廣州刺史。

translations.literal: Xiaowu commended him, again appointed him Administrator of Yingchuan Commandery, and promoted him to Governor of Guang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu praised him, reappointed him administrator of Yingchuan, and promoted him to governor of Guang province.

sentences.zh: 東魏遣行臺侯景率兵攻之，長壽衆少，城陷，遂遇害。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei sent the executive commissioner Hou Jing to lead troops to attack him; Changshou's forces were few, the city fell, and he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei sent its executive commissioner Hou Jing against him with an army; Changshou had too few men, his city fell, and he was killed.

sentences.zh: 大統元年，追贈太尉、使持節、侍中、驃騎大將軍、冀定等十二州諸軍事、定州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Datong he was posthumously awarded Grand Mentor, commissioner bearing the staff with full powers, Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, commander over the military affairs of the twelve provinces including Ji and Ding, and Governor of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Datong he was posthumously honored as Grand Mentor, commissioner with full plenipotentiary powers, Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, commander-in-chief over military affairs in twelve provinces including Ji and Ding, and governor of Ding province.

sentences.zh: 延孫亦雄武有將帥才略。

translations.literal: Yansun too was bold in war and possessed the talent and strategy of a commander.
translations.idiomatic: Yansun was likewise a formidable warrior with a commander's gifts.

sentences.zh: 少從長壽征討，以勇敢聞。

translations.literal: In his youth he followed Changshou on campaigns and was known for courage.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he campaigned with Changshou and won renown for bravery.

sentences.zh: 初為直閤將軍。

translations.literal: He first served as General of the Direct Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as a general of the Direct Gate.

sentences.zh: 賀拔勝為荊州刺史，表延孫為都督。

translations.literal: When Heba Sheng became Governor of Jing Province, he memorialized the throne to appoint Yansun as commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Heba Sheng took office as governor of Jing province, he recommended Yansun for a command.

sentences.zh: 肅清鵶路，頗有功力焉。

translations.literal: He cleared the Crow Road and achieved considerable merit thereby.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified the outlaw routes and won considerable credit in doing so.

sentences.zh: 及長壽被害，延孫乃還，收集其父之衆。

translations.literal: When Changshou was killed, Yansun then returned and gathered his father's troops.
translations.idiomatic: After Changshou was killed, Yansun came back and rallied his father's former forces.

sentences.zh: 自魏孝武西遷之後，朝士流亡。

translations.literal: After Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, court officials went into exile.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xiaowu of Wei withdrew to the west, officials of the court fled into exile.

sentences.zh: 廣陵王欣、錄尚書長孫稚、潁川王斌之、安昌王子均及建甯、江夏、隴東諸王幷百官等攜持妻子來投延孫者，延孫卽率衆衛送，並贈以珍玩，咸達關中。

translations.literal: Prince of Guangling Xin, Chief Clerk of the Records Office Changsun Zhi, Prince of Yingchuan Binzhi, Prince of Anchang Zijun, and the princes of Jianning, Jiangxia, and Longdong together with the hundred officials who came bringing wives and children to join Yansun—Yansun at once led his troops to guard and escort them, and also presented them with precious curios; all reached Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Guangling Xin, Chief Clerk of the Records Office Changsun Zhi, Prince of Yingchuan Binzhi, Prince of Anchang Zijun, the princes of Jianning, Jiangxia, and Longdong, and many other officials fled east with their families to seek Yansun's protection, he led his men to escort them, gave them precious gifts, and saw them all safely through to Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 齊神武深患之，遣行臺慕容紹宗等數道攻之。

translations.literal: Gao Huan of Qi was deeply troubled by this and sent the executive commissioner Murong Shaozong and others along several routes to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan of Northern Qi took this as a grave threat and sent the executive commissioner Murong Shaozong and others to attack him along several routes.

sentences.zh: 延孫獎勵所部出戰，遂大破之，臨陣斬其揚州刺史薛喜。

translations.literal: Yansun encouraged and roused his subordinates to go out to battle, then utterly defeated them and on the field beheaded their Governor of Yang Province, Xue Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Yansun roused his troops to battle, routed the enemy completely, and on the field slew Xue Xi, their governor of Yang province.

sentences.zh: 於是義軍更振。

translations.literal: Thereupon the loyalist armies were revived once more.
translations.idiomatic: The loyalist cause rallied anew.

sentences.zh: 乃授延孫京南行臺、節度河南諸軍事、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: Yansun was then appointed Executive Commissioner of the Capital South, controller of military affairs in Henan, and Governor of Guang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yansun was appointed executive commissioner for the capital south, given overall command of military affairs in Henan, and made governor of Guang province.

sentences.zh: 尋進車騎大將軍、儀同三司、大都督，賜爵華山郡公。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry, made Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, appointed grand commander-in-chief, and enfeoffed as Duke of Huashan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry, given the privilege of ceremonial parity with the Three Dukes, made grand commander-in-chief, and enfeoffed as Duke of Huashan.

sentences.zh: 延孫既荷重委，每以剋清伊、洛為己任。

translations.literal: Yansun, having received this weighty commission, each time took clearing the Yi and Luo regions as his own responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Entrusted with heavy responsibility, Yansun made it his personal mission to pacify the Yi and Luo region.

sentences.zh: 頻以少擊衆，威振敵境。

translations.literal: Repeatedly with few he struck many, and his prestige shook the enemy borders.
translations.idiomatic: Again and again he defeated larger forces with smaller ones, and his fame spread terror through enemy territory.

sentences.zh: 大統四年，為其長史楊伯蘭所害。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Datong he was killed by his chief clerk Yang Bolan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Datong he was murdered by his chief clerk Yang Bolan.

sentences.zh: 後贈司空、冀定等六州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously awarded Minister of Works and Governor of the six provinces including Ji and Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He was later posthumously honored as Minister of Works and governor of six provinces including Ji and Ding.

sentences.zh: 子人傑，有祖、父風。

translations.literal: His son Renjie had the manner of his grandfather and father.
translations.idiomatic: His son Renjie inherited the spirit of his grandfather and father.

sentences.zh: 官至開府儀同三司、和州刺史，改封潁川郡公。

translations.literal: He reached the office of Baron with an office equal to the Three Dukes and Governor of He Province, and his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Yingchuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the rank of a baron with an establishment equal to the Three Dukes and to the governorship of He province, and his title was changed to Duke of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 延孫弟義孫，亦官至開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Yansun's younger brother Yisun also reached the office of Baron with an establishment equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Yansun's younger brother Yisun likewise rose to a baron's establishment equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 韋祐字法保，京兆山北人也。

translations.literal: Wei You, courtesy name Fabao, was a native of Shanbei in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei You, whose courtesy name was Fabao, came from Shanbei in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 少以字行於世。

translations.literal: From youth he was known in the world by his courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was known to the world by his courtesy name rather than his given name.

sentences.zh: 世為州郡著姓。

translations.literal: For generations his family had been a prominent surname in the provinces and commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: His clan had been a leading local family for generations.

sentences.zh: 祖駢，雍州主簿。

translations.literal: His grandfather Pian was Chief Clerk of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Pian served as chief clerk of Yong province.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才，拜中書博士。

translations.literal: He was recommended as a cultivated talent and appointed Erudite of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as a cultivated talent, he was appointed erudite of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 父義，前將軍、上洛郡守。

translations.literal: His father Yi was Forward General and Administrator of Shangluo Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yi was Forward General and administrator of Shangluo commandery.

sentences.zh: 魏大統時，以法保著勳，追贈秦州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Datong era of Wei, because Fabao had shown merit, he was posthumously awarded Governor of Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wei Datong era, in recognition of Fabao's achievements, Yi was posthumously honored as governor of Qin province.

sentences.zh: 法保少好遊俠，而質直少言。

translations.literal: Fabao in youth loved roaming knights-errant, yet was plain and upright and spoke little.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Fabao loved the life of the wandering knight, yet he was plainspoken, upright, and sparing of words.

sentences.zh: 所與交遊，皆輕猾亡命。

translations.literal: Those with whom he associated were all reckless, cunning fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: His companions were reckless outlaws and desperate men.

sentences.zh: 人有急難投之者，多保存之。

translations.literal: When people in urgent distress came to him, he for the most part preserved them.
translations.idiomatic: Those who fled to him in desperate need usually found shelter with him.

sentences.zh: 雖屢被追捕，終不改其操，父沒，事母兄以孝敬聞。

translations.literal: Although repeatedly pursued and captured, he never changed his conduct; when his father died, he served his mother and elder brother with filial piety and was renowned for it.
translations.idiomatic: Though often hunted by the authorities, he never abandoned his ways; after his father's death he cared for his mother and elder brother with devoted filial piety and won renown for it.

sentences.zh: 慕李長壽之為人，遂娶長壽女，因寓居關南。

translations.literal: He admired the character of Li Changshou, and therefore married Changshou's daughter and took up residence south of the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Admiring Li Changshou's character, he married Changshou's daughter and settled south of the passes.

sentences.zh: 正光末，四方雲擾。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhenguang era turmoil rose on all sides like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Zhenguang era the empire was in turmoil on every side.

sentences.zh: 王公被難者或依之，多得全濟，以此為貴遊所德。

translations.literal: Princes and nobles who suffered calamity sometimes relied on him, and many were wholly saved; for this he was esteemed by the exalted wanderers.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and nobles in peril often found refuge with him and many were saved entirely; the great families were deeply grateful.

sentences.zh: 乃拜員外散騎侍郎，加輕車將軍。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant at the Palace Secretariat and additionally made General of the Light Chariot.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed supernumerary gentleman-attendant of the scattered cavalry and additionally made General of the Light Chariot.

sentences.zh: 及魏孝武西遷，法保從山南赴行在所。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, Fabao came from south of the mountains to the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei withdrew to the west, Fabao came from south of the mountains to join the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 除右將軍、太中大夫，封固安縣男，邑二百戶。

translations.literal: He was appointed Right General and Grand Master of Palace Counsel, enfeoffed as Baron of Gu'an County with a fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Right General and Grand Master of Palace Counsel, enfeoffed as Baron of Gu'an with a fief of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 及長壽被害，其子延孫收長壽餘衆，守禦東境。

translations.literal: When Changshou was killed, his son Yansun gathered Changshou's remaining troops and defended the eastern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: After Changshou was killed, his son Yansun rallied the remnants of his father's forces and held the eastern frontier.

sentences.zh: 朝廷恐延孫兵少不能自固，乃除法保東洛州刺史，配兵數百人，以援延孫。

translations.literal: The court feared Yansun's troops were few and he could not hold firm on his own, and therefore appointed Fabao Governor of East Luoyang Province, assigning him several hundred troops to aid Yansun.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Yansun had too few men to hold his ground, the court appointed Fabao governor of East Luoyang province and assigned him several hundred troops to reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 法保至潼關，弘農郡守韋孝寬謂法保曰：「恐子此役，難以吉還也。

translations.literal: When Fabao reached Tong Pass, Wei Xiaokuan, Administrator of Hongnong Commandery, said to Fabao: "I fear that in this campaign of yours it will be hard to return with good fortune."
translations.idiomatic: At Tong Pass, Wei Xiaokuan, administrator of Hongnong commandery, told Fabao, "I fear you will be lucky to come back alive from this mission."

sentences.zh: 」法保曰：「古人稱不入虎穴，不得虎子。

translations.literal: Fabao said: "The ancients said that one who does not enter the tiger's den cannot obtain the tiger cub."
translations.idiomatic: Fabao replied, "As the ancients said, one who will not enter the tiger's den cannot take the tiger cub."

sentences.zh: 安危之事，未可預量。

translations.literal: Matters of safety and danger cannot be measured in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Whether one lives or dies cannot be foretold.

sentences.zh: 縱為國殞身，亦非所恨。

translations.literal: Even if one dies for the state, it is not something to regret.
translations.idiomatic: Even if I die for the state, I shall have no regrets.

sentences.zh: 」遂倍道兼行。

translations.literal: Thereupon he doubled the pace and pressed on by forced marches.
translations.idiomatic: With that he pressed forward at double speed.

sentences.zh: 東魏陝州刺史劉貴以步騎千餘邀之。

translations.literal: Liu Gui, Governor of Shan Province of Eastern Wei, with more than a thousand infantry and cavalry intercepted him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gui, Eastern Wei's governor of Shan province, intercepted him with more than a thousand foot and horse.

sentences.zh: 法保命所部為圓陣，且戰且前。

translations.literal: Fabao ordered his troops to form a circular battle array and advanced while fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Fabao formed his men into a circle and fought his way forward.

sentences.zh: 數日，得與延孫兵接，乃幷勢置柵於伏流。

translations.literal: After several days he was able to join Yansun's troops, and then combining their strength they set up palisades at Fulu.
translations.idiomatic: After several days he linked up with Yansun's forces; together they built fortified camps at Fulu.

sentences.zh: 未幾，太祖追法保與延孫率衆還朝，賞勞甚厚。

translations.literal: Before long the Grand Ancestor summoned Fabao and Yansun to lead their troops back to court and rewarded and comforted them very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Grand Ancestor recalled Fabao and Yansun with their troops to court and rewarded them handsomely.

sentences.zh: 乃授法保大都督。

translations.literal: Fabao was then appointed grand commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Fabao was then made grand commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 四年，除河南尹。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Intendant of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 及延孫被害，法保乃率所部，據延孫舊柵。

translations.literal: When Yansun was killed, Fabao then led his own troops and occupied Yansun's old palisades.
translations.idiomatic: After Yansun was killed, Fabao led his men to hold Yansun's former camps.

sentences.zh: 頻與敵人交兵，每身先士卒，單馬陷陣，是以戰必被傷。

translations.literal: He frequently exchanged blows with the enemy; each time he took the lead before the soldiers, charging the formation alone on horseback, and therefore in battle he was always wounded.
translations.idiomatic: He fought the enemy again and again, always leading from the front and charging alone into the enemy ranks, and so he was wounded in nearly every battle.

sentences.zh: 嘗至關南，與東魏人戰，流矢中頸，從口中出，當時氣絕。

translations.literal: Once when he reached the region south of the passes and fought Eastern Wei men, a stray arrow struck his neck and came out through his mouth; at the time he ceased breathing.
translations.idiomatic: Once south of the passes he fought Eastern Wei troops; a stray arrow struck his neck and passed out through his mouth, and he lost consciousness on the spot.

sentences.zh: 輿至營，久之乃蘇。

translations.literal: When the litter reached camp, after a long while he revived.
translations.idiomatic: Carried back to camp, he did not revive for a long time.

sentences.zh: 九年，拜車騎大將軍、儀同三司，鎮九曲城。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry and Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, and garrisoned Jiuqu City.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was made General of Chariots and Cavalry with ceremonial parity to the Three Dukes and posted to garrison Jiuqu city.

sentences.zh: 及侯景以豫州來附，法保率兵赴景。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing came over with Yuzhou to submit, Fabao led troops to go to Jing.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing defected with Yuzhou, Fabao marched to join him.

sentences.zh: 景欲留之，法保疑其有貳心，乃固辭還所鎮。

translations.literal: Jing wished to detain him; Fabao suspected he had a divided heart and therefore firmly declined and returned to his garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing tried to keep him there, but Fabao suspected treachery and firmly refused, returning to his post.

sentences.zh: 十五年，加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，尋進爵為公。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was additionally made General of Agile Cavalry and Baron with an establishment equal to the Three Dukes; soon his rank was advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry and given a baron's establishment equal to the Three Dukes; soon afterward his title was raised to duke.

sentences.zh: 會東魏遣軍送糧饋宜陽，法保潛邀之。

translations.literal: It happened that Eastern Wei sent troops escorting grain rations to Yiyang; Fabao secretly intercepted them.
translations.idiomatic: When Eastern Wei sent a convoy to supply Yiyang with grain, Fabao ambushed it.

sentences.zh: 轉戰數十里，兵少不敵，為流矢所中，卒於陣。

translations.literal: Fighting over several tens of li, his troops were few and could not match the enemy; he was struck by a stray arrow and died on the field.
translations.idiomatic: After fighting for dozens of li his outnumbered force was overwhelmed; struck by a stray arrow, he died on the battlefield.

sentences.zh: 諡曰莊。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous name Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 子初嗣。

translations.literal: His son Chu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chu succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 建德末，位至開府儀同大將軍、閻韓防主。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jiande era he reached the office of Baron with an establishment equal to the Great General and Defender of Yanhan.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Jiande era he had risen to a baron's establishment with the rank of great general and served as defender of Yanhan.

sentences.zh: 韓雄字木蘭，河南東垣人也。

translations.literal: Han Xiong, courtesy name Mulan, was a native of Dongyuan in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xiong, whose courtesy name was Mulan, came from Dongyuan in Henan.

sentences.zh: 祖景，魏孝文時為赭陽郡守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jing, in the time of Emperor Xiaowen of Wei, was Administrator of Zheyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jing served under Emperor Xiaowen of Wei as administrator of Zheyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 雄少敢勇，膂力絕人，工騎射，有將率材略。

translations.literal: Xiong in youth was daring and brave, his physical strength surpassing other men; he was skilled in horseback archery and possessed the talent and strategy of a commander.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Xiong was bold and fearless, with extraordinary strength; he excelled at mounted archery and showed the makings of a commander.

sentences.zh: 及魏孝武西遷，雄便慷慨有立功之志。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, Xiong at once was ardent and had the will to achieve merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei withdrew to the west, Xiong was seized by a passionate desire to win distinction.

sentences.zh: 大統初，遂與其屬六十餘人於洛西舉兵，數日間，衆至千人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong he then, with more than sixty of his followers, raised troops west of Luo; within several days his host reached a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Datong era he rose in arms west of the Luo with some sixty followers; within days his force grew to a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 與河南行臺楊琚共為掎角。

translations.literal: Together with Yang Ju, Executive Commissioner of Henan, he formed pincers.
translations.idiomatic: He coordinated with Yang Ju, executive commissioner of Henan, in a pincer strategy.

sentences.zh: 每抄掠東魏，所向克獲。

translations.literal: Each time he raided Eastern Wei, wherever he went he captured booty.
translations.idiomatic: His raids into Eastern Wei territory succeeded wherever he struck.

sentences.zh: 徒衆日盛，州縣不能禦之。

translations.literal: His followers grew daily in strength, and the provinces and commanderies could not resist him.
translations.idiomatic: His following swelled daily until the local provinces and commanderies could no longer contain him.

sentences.zh: 東魏洛州刺史韓賢以狀聞，鄴乃遣其軍司慕容紹宗率兵與賢合勢討雄。

translations.literal: Han Xian, Governor of Luo Province of Eastern Wei, reported the situation; Ye then sent its army commander Murong Shaozong to lead troops and join forces with Xian to attack Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xian, Eastern Wei's governor of Luo province, reported the situation to the capital; Ye sent its army commander Murong Shaozong with troops to join Xian in suppressing Xiong.

sentences.zh: 戰數十合，雄兵略盡，兄及妻子皆為賢所獲，將以為戮。

translations.literal: After several tens of engagements Xiong's troops were nearly exhausted; his elder brother and wife and children were all captured by Xian and were about to be executed.
translations.idiomatic: After dozens of clashes Xiong's force was nearly spent; Xian captured his elder brother, wife, and children and prepared to execute them.

sentences.zh: 乃遣人告雄曰：「若雄至，皆免之。

translations.literal: He then sent someone to tell Xiong: "If Xiong comes, all will be spared."
translations.idiomatic: He sent word to Xiong: "If you surrender, they will all be spared."

sentences.zh: 」雄與其所親謀曰：「奮不顧身以立功名者，本望上申忠義，下榮親戚。

translations.literal: Xiong consulted with his close associates, saying: "Those who exert themselves without regard for body to establish fame and merit originally hope above to display loyalty and righteousness and below to bring honor to kin."
translations.idiomatic: Xiong consulted his closest followers: "Men who risk everything for glory do so hoping to prove their loyalty above and bring honor to their families below."

sentences.zh: 今若忍而不赴，人謂我何。

translations.literal: Now if I endure it and do not go, what will people say of me?
translations.idiomatic: If I hold back now, what will people say of me?

sentences.zh: 既免之後，更思其計，未為晚也。

translations.literal: After they are spared, to think again of one's plans is not too late.
translations.idiomatic: Once they are safe, I can still think of another plan—it will not be too late.

sentences.zh: 」於是，遂詣賢軍，卽隨賢還洛。

translations.literal: Thereupon he went to Xian's army and at once followed Xian back to Luo.
translations.idiomatic: With that he went to Xian's camp and returned with him to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 乃潛引賢黨，謀欲襲之。

translations.literal: He then secretly won over Xian's partisans and plotted to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly won over some of Xian's followers and plotted a surprise attack.

sentences.zh: 事泄，遁免。

translations.literal: The affair leaked out and he fled and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The plot was discovered and he fled to safety.

sentences.zh: 時太祖在弘農，雄至上謁。

translations.literal: At that time the Grand Ancestor was at Hongnong; Xiong went up to pay his respects.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor was then at Hongnong; Xiong went to present himself before him.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉之，封武陽縣侯，邑八百戶。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor commended him and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Wuyang County with a fief of eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor praised him and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Wuyang with a fief of eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 遣雄還鄉里，更圖進取。

translations.literal: He sent Xiong back to his home district to plan further advances.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Xiong home to plan the next advance.

sentences.zh: 雄乃招集義衆，進逼洛州。

translations.literal: Xiong then gathered loyalist volunteers and pressed upon Luo Province.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong rallied loyal volunteers and advanced on Luo province.

sentences.zh: 東魏洛州刺史元湛委州奔河陽，其長史孟彥舉城款附。

translations.literal: Yuan Zhan, Governor of Luo Province of Eastern Wei, abandoned the province and fled to Heyang; his chief clerk Meng Yan raised the city in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhan, Eastern Wei's governor of Luo province, abandoned his post and fled to Heyang; his chief clerk Meng Yan surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 俄而領軍獨孤信大軍繼至，雄遂從信入洛陽。

translations.literal: Before long the army commander Dugu Xin arrived with a great host; Xiong then followed Xin into Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the army commander Dugu Xin arrived with the main force, and Xiong entered Luoyang with him.

sentences.zh: 時東魏將侯景等圍蓼塢，雄擊走之。

translations.literal: At that time the Eastern Wei generals Hou Jing and others besieged Liaowu; Xiong struck and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: When Eastern Wei generals including Hou Jing besieged Liaowu, Xiong attacked and drove them away.

sentences.zh: 又從太祖戰於河橋。

translations.literal: He again followed the Grand Ancestor in battle at Heqiao.
translations.idiomatic: He also fought under the Grand Ancestor at Heqiao.

sentences.zh: 軍還，仍鎮洛西。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he still garrisoned the region west of Luo.
translations.idiomatic: After the army withdrew, he continued to hold the west of the Luo.

sentences.zh: 拜假平東將軍、東郡守，遷北中郎將。

translations.literal: He was appointed acting General Who Pacifies the East and Administrator of Dong Commandery, then promoted to General of the North Palace Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was made acting General Who Pacifies the East and administrator of Dong commandery, then promoted to North Palace Gate General.

sentences.zh: 邙山之役，太祖命雄率衆邀齊神武於隘道。

translations.literal: In the battle of Mount Mang, the Grand Ancestor ordered Xiong to lead troops to intercept Gao Huan of Qi in a narrow pass.
translations.idiomatic: At Mount Mang the Grand Ancestor ordered Xiong to ambush Gao Huan in a defile.

sentences.zh: 神武怒，命三軍併力取雄。

translations.literal: Gao Huan was enraged and ordered the three armies to combine their strength to take Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Gao Huan ordered all three armies to concentrate on capturing Xiong.

sentences.zh: 雄突圍得免。

translations.literal: Xiong broke through the encirclement and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong broke out of the encirclement and escaped.

sentences.zh: 除東徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Governor of East Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed governor of East Xu province.

sentences.zh: 太祖以雄劬勞積年，乃徵入朝，屢加賞勞。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor, because Xiong had toiled with merit for many years, then summoned him to court and repeatedly rewarded and comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xiong had served strenuously on the frontier for many years, the Grand Ancestor summoned him to court and rewarded him again and again.

sentences.zh: 復遣還州。

translations.literal: He was again sent back to his province.
translations.idiomatic: He was then sent back to his province.

sentences.zh: 東魏東雍州刺史郭叔略與雄接境，頗為邊患。

translations.literal: Guo Shulue, Governor of East Yong Province of Eastern Wei, bordered Xiong's territory and was quite a frontier menace.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Shulue, Eastern Wei's governor of East Yong province, held a neighboring post and was a persistent threat on the border.

sentences.zh: 雄密圖之，乃輕將十騎，夜入其境，伏於道側。

translations.literal: Xiong secretly plotted against him, then with light equipment took ten horsemen, entered his territory by night, and lay in ambush beside the road.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong laid a secret plan: with only ten horsemen he entered enemy territory by night and hid beside the road.

sentences.zh: 遣都督韓仕於略城東，服東魏人衣服，詐若自河陽叛投關西者。

translations.literal: He sent the commander Han Shi east of Lue City, dressed in Eastern Wei clothing, pretending to be one who had defected from Heyang to Guanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his commander Han Shi east of Lue city dressed as Eastern Wei soldiers, feigning a defection from Heyang to the west.

sentences.zh: 略出馳之，雄自後射之，再發咸中，遂斬略首。

translations.literal: Shulue came out galloping after him; Xiong from behind shot at him, both shots hitting true, and he then cut off Shulue's head.
translations.idiomatic: Shulue rode out in pursuit; Xiong shot him from behind, both arrows struck home, and he cut off Shulue's head.

sentences.zh: 除河南尹，進爵為公，加車騎大將軍、儀同三司、大都督、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Intendant of Henan, his rank advanced to duke, and he was additionally made General of Chariots and Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, grand commander-in-chief, and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was made intendant of Henan, raised to duke, and additionally given the ranks of General of Chariots and Cavalry, ceremonial parity with the Three Dukes, grand commander-in-chief, and regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 尋進驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、侍中、河南邑中正。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry, Baron with an establishment equal to the Three Dukes, Palace Attendant, and chief rectifier of Henan district.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to General of Agile Cavalry, given a baron's establishment equal to the Three Dukes, made Palace Attendant, and appointed chief rectifier of the Henan district.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，進爵新義郡公，增邑通前三千八百戶，賜姓宇文氏。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, his rank was advanced to Duke of Xinyi Commandery, his fief increased to three thousand eight hundred households in all with what came before, and he was granted the surname of the Yuwen clan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, Xiong was raised to Duke of Xinyi, his fief increased to a total of three thousand eight hundred households, and he was granted the surname Yuwen.

sentences.zh: 世宗二年，除使持節、都督、中徐虞洛四州諸軍事、中州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shizong he was appointed commissioner bearing the staff with full powers, commander, controller of military affairs in the four provinces of Zhong, Xu, Yu, and Luo, and Governor of Zhong Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shizong he was made commissioner with full plenipotentiary powers, commander over military affairs in Zhong, Xu, Yu, and Luo provinces, and governor of Zhong province.

sentences.zh: 雄久在邊，具知敵人虛實。

translations.literal: Xiong had long been on the frontier and fully knew the enemy's strengths and weaknesses.
translations.idiomatic: Long service on the frontier had taught him the enemy's strengths and weaknesses in full.

sentences.zh: 每率衆深入，不避艱難。

translations.literal: Each time he led his troops deep in, not avoiding hardship.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly led deep raids without shrinking from hardship.

sentences.zh: 前後經四十五戰，雖時有勝負，而雄志氣益壯。

translations.literal: Before and after he passed through forty-five battles; although at times there were victories and defeats, Xiong's spirit grew ever bolder.
translations.idiomatic: He fought forty-five battles in all; win or lose, his fighting spirit only grew bolder.

sentences.zh: 東魏深憚之。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei deeply feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei came to fear him deeply.

sentences.zh: 天和三年，卒于鎮。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianhe he died at his garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianhe he died at his post.

sentences.zh: 贈大將軍、中華宜義和五州諸軍事、中州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Great General, commander over military affairs in the five provinces of Zhong, Hua, Yi, Yi, and He, and Governor of Zhong Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Great General, commander-in-chief over the five provinces of Zhong, Hua, Yi, Yi, and He, and governor of Zhong province.

sentences.zh: 諡曰威。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous name Wei.

sentences.zh: 子禽嗣。

translations.literal: His son Qin succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qin succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 陳忻字永怡，宜陽人也。

translations.literal: Chen Xin, courtesy name Yongyi, was a native of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xin, whose courtesy name was Yongyi, came from Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 少驍勇，有氣俠，姿貌魁岸，同類咸敬憚之。

translations.literal: In youth he was valiant and brave, possessed chivalrous spirit, and had a towering stature; his peers all respected and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was fierce and brave, full of chivalrous spirit, and imposing in stature; his peers respected and feared him.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武西遷之後，忻乃於辟惡山招集勇敢少年數十人，寇掠東魏，仍密遣使歸附。

translations.literal: After Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, Xin then on Pibie Mountain gathered several tens of daring youths, raided Eastern Wei, and still secretly sent envoys to submit.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xiaowu of Wei withdrew to the west, Xin gathered several dozen bold young men on Mount Pibie, raided Eastern Wei, and secretly sent envoys to declare allegiance to the west.

sentences.zh: 大統元年，授持節、伏波將軍、羽林監、立義大都督，賜爵霸城縣男。

translations.literal: In the first year of Datong he was granted bearing-the-staff credentials, made General Who Subdues Waves, Supervisor of the Forest of Feathers, and Commander-in-Chief Who Raises Righteousness, and enfeoffed as Baron of Bacheng County.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Datong he received plenipotentiary credentials, was made General Who Subdues Waves, supervisor of the imperial guards, and commander of the righteous forces, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Bacheng.

sentences.zh: 三年，太祖復弘農，東魏揚州刺史段琛拔城遁走。

translations.literal: In the third year the Grand Ancestor recovered Hongnong; Duan Chen, Governor of Yang Province of Eastern Wei, abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the Grand Ancestor recovered Hongnong; Duan Chen, Eastern Wei's governor of Yang province, abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 忻率義徒於九曲道邀之，殺傷甚衆，擒其新安令張祗。

translations.literal: Xin led his righteous followers to intercept them on the Jiuqu road, killing and wounding very many, and captured their magistrate of Xin'an, Zhang Di.
translations.idiomatic: Xin ambushed them on the Jiuqu road with his volunteers, inflicting heavy casualties and capturing Zhang Di, magistrate of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉其忠款，使行新安縣事。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor commended his loyal sincerity and had him act as administrator of Xin'an County.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor praised his loyalty and put him in charge of Xin'an county.

sentences.zh: 及獨孤信入洛，忻舉李延孫為前鋒，仍從信守金墉城。

translations.literal: When Dugu Xin entered Luo, Xin nominated Li Yansun as vanguard and still followed Xin in guarding Jinyong City.
translations.idiomatic: When Dugu Xin entered Luoyang, Xin put Li Yansun at the head of the vanguard and joined Xin in holding Jinyong city.

sentences.zh: 及河橋戰不利，隨軍西還，復行新安縣事。

translations.literal: When the battle at Heqiao went badly, he followed the army west in retreat and again acted as administrator of Xin'an County.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat at Heqiao he withdrew west with the army and again administered Xin'an county.

sentences.zh: 東魏遣土人牛道恆為

translations.literal: Eastern Wei sent a local man, Niu Daoheng, to be
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei appointed the local leader Niu Daoheng as

translations.literal: (Yang)
translations.idiomatic: (Yang [in the received text])

sentences.zh: 〔陽〕州刺史，忻率兵擊破之，進爵為子。

translations.literal: [Yang] Province governor; Xin led troops and defeated him, and his rank was advanced to viscount.
translations.idiomatic: governor of Yang province; Xin attacked and defeated him and was promoted to viscount.

sentences.zh: 常隨崤東諸將鎮遏伊、洛間，每有功效。

translations.literal: He constantly followed the generals east of Xiao in garrisoning and restraining the region between the Yi and Luo, and each time had merit.
translations.idiomatic: He regularly served with the generals east of Xiao in holding the Yi–Luo corridor, and won credit in every campaign.

sentences.zh: 九年，與李遠迎高仲密，仍從戰邙山。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he joined Li Yuan in welcoming Gao Zhongmi and still followed in the battle at Mount Mang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he joined Li Yuan in receiving Gao Zhongmi's defection and fought at Mount Mang.

sentences.zh: 及大軍西還，復與韓雄等依山合勢，破東魏三城，斬其金門郡守方臺洛。

translations.literal: When the great army returned west, he again with Han Xiong and others combined their strength relying on the mountains, broke three Eastern Wei cities, and beheaded their Administrator of Jinmen Commandery, Fang Tailuo.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army withdrew west, he joined Han Xiong and others in a mountain offensive, took three Eastern Wei cities, and slew Fang Tailuo, administrator of Jinmen commandery.

sentences.zh: 增邑六百戶。

translations.literal: His fief was increased by six hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: His fief was increased by six hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋行宜陽郡事。

translations.literal: Soon he acted as administrator of Yiyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He soon took charge of Yiyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 東魏復遣劉盆生為金門郡守，忻又斬之。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei again sent Liu Pensheng as Administrator of Jinmen Commandery; Xin again beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: When Eastern Wei sent Liu Pensheng as administrator of Jinmen, Xin slew him as well.

sentences.zh: 除鎮遠將軍、魏郡守。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distant and Administrator of Wei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General Who Pacifies the Distant and administrator of Wei commandery.

sentences.zh: 俄授使持節、平東將軍、顯州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was granted commissioner bearing the staff with full powers, made General Who Pacifies the East, and appointed Governor of Xian Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made commissioner with full plenipotentiary powers, General Who Pacifies the East, and governor of Xian province.

sentences.zh: 太祖以忻威著敵境，仍留靜邊，弗令之任。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor, because Xin's prestige was manifest in enemy territory, still kept him to pacify the frontier and did not let him take up his appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xin's reputation struck fear in enemy territory, the Grand Ancestor kept him on the frontier to hold the border and would not release him to take up his new post.

sentences.zh: 十年，侯景築九曲城，忻率衆邀之，擒其宜陽郡守趙嵩、金門郡守樂敬賓。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Hou Jing built Jiuqu City; Xin led troops to intercept him and captured his Administrator of Yiyang Commandery Zhao Song and Administrator of Jinmen Commandery Yue Jingbin.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Hou Jing built Jiuqu city; Xin intercepted him and captured Zhao Song, administrator of Yiyang, and Yue Jingbin, administrator of Jinmen.

sentences.zh: 十三年，從李遠平九曲城，授帥都督。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he followed Li Yuan in pacifying Jiuqu City and was appointed commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he joined Li Yuan in taking Jiuqu city and was made commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 東魏將爾朱渾願率精騎三千來向宜

translations.literal: The Eastern Wei general Erzhu Hunyuan led three thousand elite cavalry toward Yi
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Wei general Erzhu Hunyuan led three thousand elite horsemen toward Yi

translations.literal: (cheng [city])
translations.idiomatic: (cheng [in the received text])

sentences.zh: 〔陽〕，忻與諸將輕兵邀之，願遂退走。

translations.literal: [yang]; Xin with the various generals with light troops intercepted him, and Hunyuan then retreated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yang; Xin and the other generals intercepted him with a light force, and Hunyuan withdrew.

sentences.zh: 十五年，除宜陽郡守，加大都督、撫軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was appointed Administrator of Yiyang Commandery and additionally made grand commander-in-chief and General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was made administrator of Yiyang commandery and additionally given the ranks of grand commander-in-chief and General Who Pacifies the Army.

sentences.zh: 十六年，進車騎大將軍、儀同三司、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry with ceremonial parity to the Three Dukes and made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 與齊將東方老戰于石泉，破之，俘獲甚衆。

translations.literal: He fought with the Qi general Dongfang Lao at Shiquan, defeated him, and captured very many.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the Qi general Dongfang Lao at Shiquan and took a great number of prisoners.

sentences.zh: 時東魏每歲遣兵送米饋宜陽，忻輒與諸軍邀擊之，每多剋獲。

translations.literal: At that time each year Eastern Wei sent troops escorting grain to supply Yiyang; Xin then with the various armies intercepted and struck them, each time capturing much booty.
translations.idiomatic: Each year Eastern Wei sent grain convoys to Yiyang; Xin and the other commanders ambushed them again and again with rich spoils.

sentences.zh: 忻與韓雄里閈姻婭，少相親昵。

translations.literal: Xin and Han Xiong were neighbors by village and connected by marriage; in youth they were close and intimate.
translations.idiomatic: Xin and Han Xiong were neighbors and kin by marriage and had been close since youth.

sentences.zh: 俱總兵境上三十餘載，每有禦扞，二人相赴，常若影響。

translations.literal: Both commanded troops on the frontier for more than thirty years; whenever there was defense and resistance, the two men rushed to each other, constantly like shadow and echo.
translations.idiomatic: For more than thirty years they commanded troops on the frontier; whenever danger threatened, one rushed to the other as swiftly as shadow follows form.

sentences.zh: 故得數對勍敵，而常保功名。

translations.literal: Therefore they were able repeatedly to face fierce enemies yet constantly preserve fame and merit.
translations.idiomatic: Thus they faced formidable enemies again and again yet kept their fame and fortunes intact.

sentences.zh: 雖竝有武力，至於挽強射中，忻不如雄；

translations.literal: Although both possessed martial strength, as for drawing the strong bow and hitting the target, Xin was not the equal of Xiong;
translations.idiomatic: Though both were men of great physical power, Xin could not match Xiong in drawing the heavy bow and hitting the mark;

sentences.zh: 散財施惠，得士衆心，則雄不如忻。

translations.literal: in scattering wealth and bestowing favors and winning the hearts of officers and troops, Xiong was not the equal of Xin.
translations.idiomatic: but in giving freely and winning the loyalty of his men, Xiong could not equal Xin.

sentences.zh: 身死之日，將吏荷其恩德，莫不感慟焉。

translations.literal: On the day of his death the officers and clerks, bearing his grace and virtue, none failed to be moved to grief.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, the officers and men who had benefited from his kindness were all overcome with grief.

sentences.zh: 子萬敵嗣。

translations.literal: His son Wandi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wandi succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以忻雅得士心，還令萬敵領其部曲。

translations.literal: The court, because Xin had long won the hearts of the troops, again had Wandi lead his military household.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xin had long held the loyalty of his troops, the court had Wandi take command of his old unit.

sentences.zh: 魏玄字僧智，任城人也。

translations.literal: Wei Xuan, courtesy name Sengzhi, was a native of Rencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xuan, whose courtesy name was Sengzhi, came from Rencheng.

sentences.zh: 六世祖休，仕晉為魯郡守。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Xiu served Jin as Administrator of Lu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His sixth-generation ancestor Xiu served the Jin as administrator of Lu commandery.

sentences.zh: 永嘉南遷，遂居江左。

translations.literal: At the Yongjia migration south he then dwelt in the lands east of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: At the Yongjia migration south the family settled in the lower Yangtze region.

sentences.zh: 父承祖，魏景明中，自梁歸魏，家於新安。

translations.literal: His father Chengzu, in the Jingming era of Wei, came over from Liang to Wei and made his home at Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chengzu defected from Liang to Wei in the Jingming era and settled at Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 玄少慷慨，有膽略。

translations.literal: Xuan in youth was ardent and generous and possessed courage and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Xuan was high-spirited and bold, with courage and resource.

sentences.zh: 普泰中，除奉朝請。

translations.literal: In the Putai era he was appointed Attendant at Court.
translations.idiomatic: During the Putai era he was appointed court attendant.

sentences.zh: 頻從軍與梁人交戰。

translations.literal: He frequently followed the army in exchanges of battle with the men of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned repeatedly against Liang.

sentences.zh: 永安初，以功授征虜將軍、中散大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yong'an, for merit he was appointed General Who Captures Barbarians and Palace Attendant of the Central Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Yong'an era he was rewarded with the ranks of General Who Captures Barbarians and palace attendant of the central scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 及魏孝武西遷，東魏北徙，人情騷動，各懷去就。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west and Eastern Wei shifted north, popular sentiment was agitated and each person harbored thoughts of staying or leaving.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei withdrew west and Eastern Wei moved its capital north, the people were unsettled and everyone weighed whether to stay or go.

sentences.zh: 玄遂率募鄉曲，立義于關南，卽從韋法保與東魏司徒高敖曹戰於關口。

translations.literal: Xuan then led recruited local militia and raised righteousness south of the passes, and at once followed Wei Fabao in battle against Gao Aocao, Minister of Works of Eastern Wei, at the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan raised a loyal militia south of the passes and fought with Wei Fabao against Gao Aocao, Eastern Wei's Minister of Works, at the pass.

sentences.zh: 及獨孤信入洛陽，隸行臺楊琚防馬渚。

translations.literal: When Dugu Xin entered Luoyang, he was attached to Yang Ju, Executive Commissioner, in defending Mazhu.
translations.idiomatic: When Dugu Xin entered Luoyang, he served under the executive commissioner Yang Ju in defending Mazhu.

sentences.zh: 復與高敖曹接戰。

translations.literal: He again joined in battle with Gao Aocao.
translations.idiomatic: He fought Gao Aocao again.

sentences.zh: 自是每率鄉兵，抗拒東魏。

translations.literal: From this time he each time led local militia to resist Eastern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he led local militia against Eastern Wei again and again.

sentences.zh: 前後十餘戰，皆有功。

translations.literal: Before and after, in more than ten battles, all had merit.
translations.idiomatic: In more than ten engagements he won credit every time.

sentences.zh: 邙山之役，大軍不利，宜陽、洛州皆為東魏守。

translations.literal: In the campaign at Mount Mang the great army was unfavored; Yiyang and Luo Province were both held by Eastern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat at Mount Mang, Yiyang and Luo province fell into Eastern Wei hands.

sentences.zh: 崤東立義者，咸懷異望。

translations.literal: The righteous forces east of Xiao all harbored divergent ambitions.
translations.idiomatic: The loyalist leaders east of Xiao began to waver in their allegiance.

sentences.zh: 而玄母及弟並在宜陽。

translations.literal: Yet Xuan's mother and younger brother were both in Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Xuan's mother and younger brother were both in Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 玄以為忠孝不兩立，及率義徒還關南鎮撫。

translations.literal: Xuan considered that loyalty and filial piety cannot both stand, and thereupon led his righteous followers back to pacify and reassure the region south of the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan believed loyalty and filial duty could not both be fully honored, and he led his volunteers back south of the passes to hold the frontier.

sentences.zh: 太祖手書勞之，除洛陽令，封廣宗縣子，邑四百戶。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor by his own hand wrote to comfort him, appointed him Magistrate of Luoyang, and enfeoffed him as Viscount of Guangzong County with a fief of four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor wrote him a personal letter of praise, appointed him magistrate of Luoyang, and enfeoffed him as Viscount of Guangzong with a fief of four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 十三年，與開府李義孫攻拔伏流城，又剋孔城，卽與義孫鎮之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, together with Li Yisun, Baron with an establishment, he attacked and took Fulu City, and again captured Kong City; he then with Yisun garrisoned them.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he and Li Yisun took Fulu city and then Kong city, which they garrisoned together.

sentences.zh: 尋移鎮伏流。

translations.literal: Soon he shifted his garrison to Fulu.
translations.idiomatic: He soon moved his headquarters to Fulu.

sentences.zh: 十四年，授帥都督、東平郡守，轉河南郡守，加大都督。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was appointed commander-in-chief and Administrator of Dongping Commandery, transferred to Administrator of Henan Commandery, and additionally made grand commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was made commander-in-chief and administrator of Dongping commandery, then transferred to administrator of Henan and promoted to grand commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 十六年，洛安民雍方雋據郡外叛，率步騎一千，自號行臺，攻破郡縣，囚執守令。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Yong Fangjun of Luo'an, holding territory outside the commandery in rebellion, led a thousand infantry and cavalry, styled himself executive commissioner, broke commanderies and counties, and imprisoned and seized the administrators and magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year Yong Fangjun of Luo'an rebelled outside the commandery seat with a thousand foot and horse, declared himself an executive commissioner, overran the districts, and seized the local officials.

sentences.zh: 玄率弘農、九曲、孔城、伏流四城士馬討平之。

translations.literal: Xuan led the troops and horses of the four cities of Hongnong, Jiuqu, Kongcheng, and Fulu to campaign and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan led the forces of Hongnong, Jiuqu, Kong city, and Fulu and put down the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝二年，拜車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Gong of Wei he was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry and Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Gong of Wei he was made General of Chariots and Cavalry with ceremonial parity to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：二國爭強，四郊多壘，鎮守要害，義屬武臣。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: The two states strove for supremacy; on all four borders ramparts were many; to garrison strategic points was the proper duty of military officers.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: As the two realms struggled for mastery and fortresses multiplied along every border, holding the vital passes fell by right to men of war.

sentences.zh: 李延孫等以勇略之姿，受扞城之寄。

translations.literal: Li Yansun and others, with bearing of courage and strategy, received the charge of defending cities.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Li Yansun, endowed with courage and stratagem, were entrusted with the defense of the frontier fortresses.

sentences.zh: 灌瓜贈藥，雖有愧於昔賢；

translations.literal: Offering melons and presenting medicine—although they fell short of the worthies of old;
translations.idiomatic: They may not have matched the old stories of generals exchanging melons and medicine across the lines;

sentences.zh: 禦侮折沖，足方駕於前烈。

translations.literal: in repelling insult and breaking the enemy assault, they were fully able to drive abreast of former exemplars.
translations.idiomatic: yet in repelling invasion and breaking the enemy's charge they stood fully equal to the heroes of earlier ages.

sentences.zh: 用能觀兵伊、洛，保據崤、函，齊人沮西略之謀，周朝緩東顧之慮，皆數將之力也。

translations.literal: By this they were able to display arms at the Yi and Luo, hold and secure Xiao and Han, make the men of Qi frustrate their plan of advancing west, and ease the Zhou court's concern of looking east—all through the power of these several generals.
translations.idiomatic: They kept armies on the Yi and Luo, held Xiao and Han, blunted Qi's designs in the west, and eased the Zhou court's fear of the east—all through the strength of these commanders.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七一年十一月版《周書》為本校。

translations.literal: The full text takes as its collated standard the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Zhou, November 1971.
translations.idiomatic: This full text has been collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Zhou (November 1971).
